candidates.title: Cyborg insects as building search-and-rescue infrastructure
candidates.shift: Insect-robot hybrids equipped with sensors and needle-actuators are being prototyped for post-disaster search and rescue inside collapsed structures.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could reshape emergency-response equipment standards for building collapse and insurance/rescue protocols; strange because it blurs biology and robotics inside the built environment.
candidates.evidence: IEEE Spectrum prototype 'Paraborg' cyborg cockroach with spring-loaded needle for delivering aid in rubble.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of biology-robotics hybrids entering disaster response, driven by miniaturized sensing/actuation; if scaled, could change emergency-service equipment and insurance protocols for building-collapse scenarios.
candidates.author: Charles Q. Choi

candidates.title: Anti-AI design objects as physical countertrend
candidates.shift: A wave of designed objects and spaces intentionally reject AI-driven interfaces, restoring manual control to users.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: early consumer/design backlash that could shape store experience design toward deliberately 'de-automated' or manual-control retail aesthetics as a counter to AI-heavy store tech.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen roundup of five designs explicitly pushing back against AI in daily life.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from techno-optimist design toward intentional de-automation, driven by AI fatigue; if it spreads, retailers may need to offer 'human-only' or manual-control store experiences as differentiators.
candidates.author: Amy Peacock

candidates.title: Retail brand extends into permanent housing/community development
candidates.shift: A streetwear retail brand (CARNIVAL) has built a housing project in Bangkok blending brand identity with residential/community space.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: retailers moving from store-only footprint into owned community/residential real estate, blurring retail and property development.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily profile of 'Housing CARNIVAL' by Studio Profile, brand-driven residential development in Bangkok.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of a retail brand acting as real-estate developer, driven by brand-community building; if it spreads, mass retailers could develop mixed residential/commercial 'brand villages' instead of standalone stores.
candidates.author: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang

candidates.title: Smart micro-space design normalizing shrinking floor plates
candidates.shift: Research on optimizing compact bedrooms via smart/digital integration reflects broader urban housing downsizing pressure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: as housing units shrink, adjacent commercial/retail real estate (ground-floor retail, storage needs) may need compact, multi-use store formats to match.
candidates.evidence: Civil Engineering and Architecture paper on smart built environment space optimization for compact bedrooms.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from static room design to tech-integrated flexible micro-space, driven by urban density; could presage similarly flexible/compact store or dark-store formats within shrinking urban footprints.
candidates.author: Shuai Bu, Ruzinoor Che Mat

candidates.title: Mega-event venues repurposed as permanent accommodation stock
candidates.shift: Analysis of how temporary Olympic accommodation structures convert to permanent housing/commercial use post-event.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: a repeatable model for adaptive reuse of large temporary structures, relevant to how big-box/pop-up retail real estate could be designed for planned conversion.
candidates.evidence: Research Square paper analyzing temporary-to-permanent accommodation models in contemporary mega-events.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of 'designed-for-conversion' construction philosophy, driven by cost/sustainability pressure on one-off mega-structures; if adopted, retail construction could similarly be designed for planned repurposing.
candidates.author: Valerio della Sala

candidates.title: Decentralized water economy substitutes for failed municipal infrastructure
candidates.shift: In Mexican cities, drinking water is increasingly delivered via trucks, bottles, rooftop tanks, and informal networks rather than public mains.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a peripheral-geography case where informal decentralized infrastructure becomes the norm; retailers in such markets may need on-site water resilience as standard, not exception.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily profile 'Rain Rhizome' describing Mexican urban water substitution economy (trucks, garrafones, rooftop tanks).
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from centralized to decentralized/informal water provisioning as climate and infrastructure failure deepen; if it spreads, retail real-estate operators may need to budget for private water sourcing/storage as a core utility line.
candidates.author: Valentina Díaz

candidates.title: Mass timber becomes standard for peripheral public infrastructure
candidates.shift: A regional Brazilian airport uses glued laminated timber (glulam) tied to local agro-industrial identity, reducing carbon footprint.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: peripheral geography adopting advanced low-carbon construction ahead of many Western peers; could signal glulam becoming viable for large-format retail/warehouse structures in emerging markets.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily profile of Doutor Leite Lopes State Airport by Bacco Arquitetos, glulam structure.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of periphery-led adoption of sustainable construction material for large public infrastructure; if it spreads, mass-market retailers could source glulam for warehouse/big-box construction in similar regions.
candidates.author: Nana Dokua
